title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 17
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 17: the burden of Damascus, the thinned glory of Jacob, gleanings on the olive tree, and nations that roar like the seas.

questions.text: What will Damascus become according to verse 1?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.

questions.text: What will the forsaken cities of Aroer be for?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says the cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be for flocks, which will lie down with no one to make them afraid.

questions.text: What will happen to the glory of Jacob in that day?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.

answers.text: It will shine like the sun
It will be carried to Babylon
It will fill the whole earth

questions.text: How many olives are left in the top of the uppermost bough?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says gleanings will be left, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives in the top of the uppermost bough.

questions.text: To whom will people look in that day?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says that in that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.

questions.text: What will people no longer look to in that day?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says they will not look to the altars, the work of their hands, neither the Asherah poles nor the incense altars.

answers.text: The altars, the work of their hands

questions.text: What does verse 10 say the people have forgotten?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength.

answers.text: The covenant made with their fathers
The words of their own prophets
The feasts of the new moon

questions.text: What happens to the harvest of the pleasant plants?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says the seed blossoms in the morning, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

answers.text: It flees away in the day of grief

questions.text: What is the roaring of the many peoples compared to?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says the many peoples roar like the roaring of the seas, and the nations rush like the rushing of mighty waters.

answers.text: The crackling of thorns in a fire

questions.text: What becomes of the plunderers between evening and morning?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says, "At evening, behold, terror! Before the morning, they are no more." This is the portion of those who plunder us.

answers.text: By morning they take the city
Before the morning, they are no more
